title: Distinguish update sentinels from stored values
applies_when: A caller passes negative, null or omitted fields into a persistence helper, and a lead alleges that existing limits or configuration will be overwritten.
lesson: Read every relevant backend setter before treating a request object as the stored result. A sentinel can mean leave the existing field unchanged, even when that same value represents unlimited in a newly created record. At JuiceFS's cited revision, ScanUserGroupUsage passes MaxSpace/MaxInodes=-1, but Redis and KV setters merge nonnegative fields into the existing quota; SQL does the same through updateQuotaFields. This refutes the persistent-limit-overwrite explanation, not all scan defects. Test an existing record with nondefault limits through the real public operation and read it back, with a new-record control when creation semantics matter. Observe process-local caches separately and trace their refresh and actual callers before attributing a durable or user-visible failure.
avoid_when: Do not generalize -1 or null semantics to another helper, field, backend or revision. A correct persistent merge does not prove cache freshness, atomicity, concurrency safety, missing-record behavior or error recovery. Source inspection of all setters is not native qualification of all engines. A cache snapshot without a supported caller and observable operation is not an enforcement vulnerability. This lesson does not establish Scout accuracy or PR yield.

evidence.note: ScanUserGroupUsage constructs usage entries with negative limit fields and rebuilds local maps. Request fields and local cache state must be distinguished from persisted setter results. Source evidence only.
doSetQuota loads the original quota and replaces each limit only when the incoming value is nonnegative; doDelQuota is a separate operation. Not a live Redis test.
doSetQuota merges nonnegative fields into a parsed existing record, initializing missing-record limits separately. Source semantics, not qualification of every KV backend.
updateQuotaFields preserves an existing negative-sentinel field but handles nonexistent rows separately. Both directory and user/group setters use it. Source evidence, not a SQL-engine test matrix.
